questions.question: Your manager asks for a quick update on a task. Which message is most effective?
options: "Working on it, will update you soon when there's progress."
"Login API done; tests 80% complete; on track for Friday. No blockers."
"Lots happened today, will explain everything in detail later."
"Almost finished, just some small issues left, should be fine."
questions.explanation: A good status update is specific and concise: what is done, what remains, the expected date and any blockers.

questions.question: During a requirements call, a stakeholder describes a feature quickly. What is the best way to show active listening?
options: Paraphrase what you heard and ask whether it is correct
Stay silent and start coding right after the call
Interrupt to suggest a different technical approach
Nod along and rely on remembering the details later
questions.explanation: Paraphrasing confirms understanding and surfaces gaps early, a core active-listening technique.

questions.question: Which email subject line is most useful to a busy team lead?
options: "Hi"
"Regarding the thing we discussed earlier"
"URGENT!!! PLEASE READ IMMEDIATELY"
"Action needed by Wed: approve DB schema change"
questions.explanation: A clear subject states the action and deadline, helping recipients prioritise without opening the mail.

questions.question: You are stuck on a bug for two hours. What is the best way to ask a senior colleague for help?
options: Say "my code doesn't work, can you check?"
Keep trying alone for several more days
Share the error, what you tried, and what you expect
Post the entire codebase and ask them to fix it
questions.explanation: A focused question with context and attempted steps respects the helper's time and speeds resolution.

questions.question: After a team meeting, what is the most useful follow-up communication?
options: Assume everyone remembers what was agreed
Send a summary with decisions, owners and deadlines
Send the full raw transcript to all attendees
Discuss outcomes only with your close teammates
questions.explanation: A written summary of decisions and action items creates shared accountability and avoids misunderstandings.

questions.question: You must explain a server outage to a non-technical client. What is the best approach?
options: Explain the impact and fix in plain language, avoiding jargon
Use detailed technical terms to sound credible
Avoid explaining and just say it is resolved
Forward the internal engineering logs directly
questions.explanation: Tailoring the message to the audience means focusing on impact, resolution and next steps in plain language.

questions.question: You realise you will miss a deadline in three days. When should you inform your lead?
options: On the deadline day if it is still not done
Only if the lead asks about progress
After the deadline, once the task is finished
Now, with the reason and a proposed new plan
questions.explanation: Early, transparent communication with a proposed plan lets the team adjust before the risk becomes a problem.

questions.question: You need a detailed design decision documented for the team. Which channel is best?
options: A one-to-one voice call with one teammate
A quick emoji reaction in the group chat
A shared document or ticket, linked in the team channel
A personal note saved on your laptop
questions.explanation: Important decisions belong in persistent, searchable shared documentation so the whole team can refer to them.

questions.question: A teammate's pull request has several issues. Which review comment is most constructive?
options: "This code is bad, please rewrite it properly."
"This loop re-queries the DB each time; caching the result outside may fix the slowness."
"I would never write it like this myself."
"Looks fine overall," despite seeing the problems.
questions.explanation: Constructive feedback is specific, about the work not the person, and suggests an improvement.

questions.question: Your lead criticises your report's structure in a review. What is the most professional response?
options: Ask clarifying questions and agree on specific improvements
Defend every choice to show you were right
Accept silently but change nothing afterwards
Complain to peers that the review was unfair
questions.explanation: Receiving feedback well means seeking to understand it and turning it into concrete actions.

questions.question: In a meeting, a senior colleague proposes an approach you believe has a security flaw. What should you do?
options: Stay silent because they are more senior
Mock the idea to make your point stronger
Implement your own approach without telling anyone
Respectfully raise the concern with evidence and suggest an alternative
questions.explanation: Raising concerns respectfully with evidence supports good decisions and psychological safety.

questions.question: Which practice makes a project README most useful to new team members?
options: Long paragraphs on the project's history only
Only a list of every file in the repository
Clear setup steps, examples and who to contact for help
Internal jokes that only current members understand
questions.explanation: Good documentation is task-oriented: how to set up, how to use, and where to get help.

questions.question: A client asks for a feature 'by tomorrow' that needs a week. What is the best response?
options: Agree to tomorrow and work overnight to try
Explain the estimate, and offer a smaller deliverable for tomorrow
Refuse without giving any explanation
Ignore the request until your manager responds
questions.explanation: Honest estimates plus options manage expectations and maintain trust.

questions.question: You lead a remote stand-up where a few people dominate. What best improves participation?
options: Go round each member with a fixed short time per update
Let the most vocal people continue as usual
Cancel stand-ups and rely on chat only
Ask only the manager to speak in each meeting
questions.explanation: A structured round-robin gives everyone equal voice and keeps the stand-up focused.

questions.question: A teammate sounds frustrated while describing a blocker. What is the best first response?
options: Tell them frustration is unprofessional
Immediately change the topic to your own work
Advise them to just work harder
Acknowledge their frustration and ask what would help
questions.explanation: Acknowledging emotion before problem-solving builds trust and opens productive conversation.

questions.question: You have 10 minutes to demo a feature to managers. Which structure works best?
options: Walk through every line of code in order
Start with a long history of the project
State the problem, show the solution, then the impact and next steps
Show random features as you remember them
questions.explanation: A problem-solution-impact structure keeps a short demo relevant to a managerial audience.

questions.question: A dependency team has not answered your requests for a week, blocking a release. What is the best next step?
options: Publicly blame the other team in a company channel
Inform your lead with the facts and impact, and request escalation
Keep waiting silently until they reply
Quietly work around it by copying their code
questions.explanation: Escalating through the proper channel with facts and impact is professional and gets the blocker resolved.

questions.question: Two teammates argue in chat about code style, and it is getting personal. As the person they both respect, what should you do?
options: Suggest moving to a call and agreeing on a team style guide
Pick a side publicly to end the argument
Ignore it and hope it resolves itself
Report both to HR immediately
questions.explanation: De-escalating to a synchronous conversation and focusing on an objective standard resolves the issue without blame.

questions.question: You work with an overseas team in a different time zone. What best avoids misunderstanding?
options: Use local slang to sound friendly
Schedule all meetings in your own working hours
Assume silence means agreement
Write clear asynchronous updates and confirm key points in writing
questions.explanation: Clear written async communication and explicit confirmation reduce ambiguity across time zones and cultures.

questions.question: During a production outage, what should regular stakeholder updates contain?
options: Detailed blame of who caused the issue
Only a final message after everything is fixed
Current impact, actions in progress, and time of next update
Speculation about root causes as facts
questions.explanation: Incident communication best practice is regular, factual updates on impact, actions and the next update time.

questions.question: You want the team to adopt automated testing. Which approach is most persuasive?
options: Insist it is obviously better than current practice
Present data on recent bugs and a small pilot plan
Add tests secretly and force them in later
Wait until a major failure proves your point
questions.explanation: Evidence plus a low-risk pilot addresses concerns and makes adoption easy to agree to.

questions.question: A senior from another team asks you to take urgent extra work while you are on a committed sprint task. What is best?
options: Explain your current commitment and involve your lead to prioritise
Accept it and quietly drop your sprint task
Refuse rudely because it is not your team
Accept and do both by working all night
questions.explanation: Transparently surfacing the trade-off and letting the lead prioritise protects commitments and relationships.
